ELMALILI:1:2#5/r1.anchor: Kur’an “Rabbu’l-‘avâlim” demiyor da “Rabbü’l-âlemîn” diyor ve bununla bilhassa zevi’l-‘ukūlü tağlib ederek onların nazar-ı dikkatini celb eyliyor

ELMALILI:1:2#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r2.claim: The plural’s focus on rational consciousness, reinforced by the merciful and sovereign attributes, draws reason from unseen knowledge to witnessed presence and the direct covenant of worship.
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r2.anchor: şu‘ûr-i ‘ukalâyı gāibden şuhûda getirip إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ diye hitab ile ‘arz-ı tevhîd u mîsâka sevk edecektir

ELMALILI:1:2#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r3.claim: Rab is a verbal noun for nurturing, applied emphatically to the nurturer; rububiyyah names this relation.
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r3.anchor: “Rab” aslında terbiye mânasına bir masdar olduğu hâlde mübalağa kasdıyla mürebbîye ıtlak edilmiştir

ELMALILI:1:2#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r4.claim: Rab entails complete power to nurture, govern, guide, command, reward, and discipline, and also means owner; without a qualifying relation it is reserved for God.
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r4.anchor: sâde mâlik veya sâde terbiye mefhumları değil, ikisine de bütün levâzımıyla sâhip olan bir kādir-i kayyûm anlaşılır

ELMALILI:1:2#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r5.claim: Nurturing is gradual movement toward perfection, visibly at work throughout the universe; contemplating the realms reveals the law of divine nurturing, while the realms themselves are known through their relation to God.
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r5.anchor: Âlemînin her kısmında ise terbiye ve tekâmül kanunlarının cereyânı her an ve her lahza meşhuddur

ELMALILI:1:2#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r6.speaker: bir kısım felâsife
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r6.claim: Some philosophers say the whole cosmos came to be all at once, with or without causes, rather than through gradual development.
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r6.anchor: bunlardan bir kısmı hepsinin def‘î olarak sebepli veya sebepsiz birdenbire tekevvün etmiş bulunduğunu

ELMALILI:1:2#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r7.speaker: bir kısım felâsife
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r7.claim: Another group denies origination by claiming that the present cosmic order has existed eternally; on this view there is no real progress, striving, or acquisition.

ELMALILI:1:2#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r8.claim: Daily observation and inference show that things arise gradually and disappear gradually; examples from geology, plants, animals, and human development contradict those denials.
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r8.anchor: efrâd-ı eşyânın, dün yok iken ufacıktan hudûsa gelip tedrîcen büyüdüğünü ve bilakis yine tedrîcen kaybolup gittiğini her gün bi’t-tecribe görüyoruz

ELMALILI:1:2#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r9.claim: The changing stages of the cosmos and human life still disclose a continuous, powerful reality that binds them and gives the observer awareness of unity.
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r9.anchor: bütün bu cereyanları izhar ve rabt ederek bize dâima vahdet şuurunu veren kādir-i kayyûm bir hakikat her dem, her lahza i‘lân-ı vücûd ediyor

ELMALILI:1:2#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r10.claim: The sign in al-alamin, later clarified by al-Baqara’s description of the Qur’an as guidance for the Godfearing, signals the wisdom of revelation.
ELMALILI:1:2#5/r10.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’nın başında هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ nazm-ı celîlinde tebeyyün edecek olan bu işâret-i mücmele

ELMALILI:1:2#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r1.claim: Observation, experience, and reason jointly establish origination and development; science may affirm evolution, but it must recognize God as its complete first cause.
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r1.anchor: Âlemde halk, terbiye, ıstıfâ ve tekâmül bir sünnet-i câriye

ELMALILI:1:2#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r2.claim: Some misuse evolutionary language by treating nature’s law as an uncaused absolute, displacing divine nurturing and making humanity the absolute summit of existence.
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r2.anchor: bunlar bu tekâmülü Hak teâlâ’nın bir eser-i terbiyesi telakkī etmeyip, müessirsiz, illetsiz olarak tabiatta bizzat cârî

ELMALILI:1:2#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r3.claim: Science depends on causality: what comes into existence after not existing must have a cause, since nothing can arise from nothing.
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r3.anchor: yok iken var olabilenin her hâlde bir sebebi vardır

ELMALILI:1:2#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r4.claim: Cause and effect must be proportionate: an effect cannot exceed its complete cause, and known effects disclose their cause; otherwise nonbeing would produce being.
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r4.anchor: ma‘lûlât ne kadar çok olursa olsun mecmû‘u illetin kudretini tecavüz edemezler, onunla mütenâsib olurlar

ELMALILI:1:2#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r5.claim: Consciousness, knowledge, and reason cannot have a blind force or blind nature as their complete cause; natural laws require an intelligent necessary being.
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r5.anchor: Hâdisâtta şuur, ilim, akıl gibi ma‘lûlât meşhud olup dururken

ELMALILI:1:2#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r6.claim: The wheat seed’s multiplication illustrates that one cannot explain the many grains by the seed’s isolated capacity alone; each added stage receives perfection from beyond itself.
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r6.anchor: bir buğday danesi toprağa düşer ve şerâitini bulunca biter, açılır, büyür, sümbüllenir, nihâyet bir başakta yüz buğday tanesi verebilir

ELMALILI:1:2#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r7.claim: The law of development therefore describes educative growth supplied from beyond each stage, not self-sufficient natural evolution; what is deficient cannot produce the complete on its own.
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r7.anchor: gelen bir kemâl vardır. Bu ise tekâmül-i tabî‘î değil, tekâmül-i terbiyevîdir

ELMALILI:1:2#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r8.speaker: Spencer
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r8.claim: Even Spencer, treated as a leading formulator of natural evolution, says an Absolute must exist beyond finite natural development, though human knowledge cannot encompass it.
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r8.anchor: feylesof Spencer[^60] bile bunun için mutlakın vücûdu zarûrî olduğunu

ELMALILI:1:2#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r9.claim: Those who deny divine nurturing contradict themselves by investing effort in education and child-rearing, which presuppose that development can be guided.
ELMALILI:1:2#6/r9.anchor: bunlar kendi kanâ‘at-i ameliyelerinde bu nazariyelerini her gün, her lahza cerh ve nakz eyliyorlar

ELMALILI:1:2#7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#7/r1.claim: Knowledge begins from a single unpartnered Truth and tests every conclusion by relating it to that highest Truth; without this relation, nature and evolution cannot be affirmed as real.
ELMALILI:1:2#7/r1.anchor: ilim her şeyden evvel hiç şerîki olmayan bir Hak tanır ve dâima vahdet mikyâsıyla yürür

ELMALILI:1:2#7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#7/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#7/r2.claim: Absolute knowledge is God’s eternal knowledge and self-disclosure; human knowledge is only a relative, contingent disclosure of that truth.
ELMALILI:1:2#7/r2.anchor: İlm-i mutlak zât-ı Hakk’ın kendine tecellîsi ve O’nun ilm-i kadîmidir

ELMALILI:1:2#7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#7/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#7/r3.claim: Without God’s perfect lordship and nurturing, neither existence nor development could be real; the world’s real share in these qualities reveals God as Lord of all realms.
ELMALILI:1:2#7/r3.anchor: Âlem ve biz böyle değilsek bir hisse-i vücûdumuz, bir hisse-i kemâlimiz, bir hisse-i terbiyemiz, hakkiyet isnad edilecek bir izâfetle bize tecellî ediyorsa

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r1.claim: The world is the collection of all things other than God that point to Him through causal relations; any part possessing an ordered relation can be called a realm.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r1.anchor: Allah’ın mâsivâsı olup illiyet alâkasıyla Allah’a delâlet eden eşyânın mecmû‘u ve bir nizâm-ı ictimâ‘îyi hâiz bulunan her kısmı âlem

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r2.claim: Alam derives from the idea of a means of knowledge and is a collective noun; it is not applied to a wholly isolated individual.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r2.anchor: مَا يُعْلَمُ بِهِ yani vesîle-i ilim mefhûmunu ifade eden “âlem” kelimesi “alem”, “alâmet” maddesinden

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r3.claim: The sound rational plural and the definite article extend the meaning across all realms and foreground rational beings; understanding the Lord of the worlds requires conceiving rational agents.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r3.anchor: cem‘-i âkil getirilmesi de ukalâ kısmının tağlîbine delâlet eyler ve ukalâyı tasavvur etmeden Rabbü’l-âlemîn iyi idrak olunamayacağını ifham eyler

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r4.claim: True knowledge is not mere conception but assent to the real relation between what is conceived; the ordered events we perceive become signs through this truth-consciousness.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r4.anchor: Asıl ilim ise tasavvur değil tasdîk-i haktır

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r5.claim: Every ordered community of things, from inner awareness to external objects, is named a realm because it serves as a sign and means of knowing God’s creation, lordship, and perfection.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r5.anchor: her cemâ‘at-i eşyâ ve bütün cemâ‘ât-i eşyâ Hak teâlâ’ya

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r6.claim: For those who truly witness, nothing is seen without God also being seen behind, before, or with it; the world is other-than-God and God lies beyond it.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r6.anchor: Ehl-i şuhûd için âlemde bir şey yoktur ki görülsün de arkasında ondan evvel veya ondan sonra, onunla beraber Allah teâlâ görülmesin

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r7.claim: Signs of God’s unity may be immediate or detailed, sensory or imagined, and can be read through perception, memory, and reason; all require conscious attention.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r7.anchor: Bu delâlet de mücmel, mufassal ve her biri şuhûdî, hayâlî olmak

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r8.claim: We know things through conscious attention and the representations it produces, yet we also judge external entities to possess objective reality beyond those representations.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r8.anchor: biz eşyâyı şuurlarımızın ta‘allukuyla şuhûden ve bu ta‘alluktan hâsıl olan suretlerle, hatıralarla tasavvuren ve aklen tanırız

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r9.claim: Judging the self, consciousness, and external objects as truly corresponding already presupposes an encompassing necessary truth that guarantees their relations; this tacit attribution to God grounds our judgments.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r9.anchor: ben bütün bunlardan evvel ve bütün bunların mâverâsında, önünde sonunda, beraberinde enfüsî ve âfâkī emkine ve ezmânı

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r10.claim: The soul cannot itself be the ultimate cause of all truth: it acknowledges its limitations and does not claim to create at will or to have existed eternally.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r10.anchor: ben öyle olsaydım her istediğimi yapar ve sana ezelden beri hiçbir yokluk göstermezdim

ELMALILI:1:2#8/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r11.claim: Even the basic judgment I exist depends on affirming a true relation between self-awareness and being, which rests on God’s encompassing truth; all limited knowledge is thereby God’s gift.
ELMALILI:1:2#8/r11.anchor: ben kendimi duyarken, önümden, sonumdan, zâhirimden, bâtınımdan muhît olan hakkı ve izâfet-i hakkı beraberimde olarak tasdik etmiş

ELMALILI:1:2#9/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r1.claim: The certainty I exist requires consciousness, and the truth of that self-awareness is guaranteed by the necessary testimony of the sovereign God, the beginning and end of every certainty.
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r1.anchor: Bu da Vâcibu’l-vücûd, hâkim-i mutlak bir Zât-ı Hakk’ın zarûrî bir tasdîkiyle, şehâdetiyle bedîhîdir

ELMALILI:1:2#9/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r2.speaker: bazıları; bazıları
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r2.claim: Some call the Creator’s existence self-evident in a clear way, others self-evident but hidden, and others demonstrative; its appearance depends on each person’s strength of self-awareness.
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r2.anchor: bazıları vücûd-i Bârî’ye bedîhî-i celî, bazıları bedîhî-i hafî

ELMALILI:1:2#9/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r3.claim: The world is a sign of God, while God is its witness and light; the cited verses describe Him as the light of heaven and earth, witness over all, and first and last.
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r3.anchor: âlem O’nun delili iken O da âlemin şâhidi, nûrudur

ELMALILI:1:2#9/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r4.claim: Faith is assent to this light, and Islam is living out that assent and relation to God.
ELMALILI:1:2#9/r4.anchor: İman bu nûra iz‘ân, dîn-i İslâm da bu iz‘ânı, bu izâfeti yaşamaktır

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r1.claim: The hymn of praise begins the sura’s actual text and gives it the alternative name al-Ḥamd.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r1.anchor: Mit dieser hymnischen Preisung, nach der die Sure auch mit ihrem alternativen Namen al-Ḥamd benannt ist, beginnt der eigentliche Text

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r2.claim: The doxology was already used in the early Meccan period; in middle Meccan texts it is joined to the epithet rabb al-ʿālamīn, itself attested early.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die Doxologie al-ḥamdu li-llāh war bereits frühmekkanisch (so in Q 52:48) in Gebrauch

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r3.speaker: Paret
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r3.claim: Paret takes ʿālamīn primarily as people, translating the epithet as Lord of people throughout the world or Lord of the world’s inhabitants.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r3.anchor: Paret (KKK, S. 12) betont, daß dabei zumeist an die Herrschaft Gottes über die Menschen gedacht ist

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r4.claim: Paret’s rendering may be factually right but omits the eschatological force; rabb an-nās would have expressed simply Lord of people.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r4.anchor: Das mag sachlich richtig sein, doch blendet diese Wiedergabe die eschatologische Dimension des Ausdrucks aus

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r5.claim: Rabb al-ʿālamīn corresponds to Jewish liturgical ribbon ʿōlām, an eschatological title spanning this world and the next; a Syriac parallel itself lacks that connotation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r5.anchor: Vielmehr entspricht das Epithet rabb al-ʿālamīn dem aus der jüdischen Liturgie bekannten hebräischen ribbon ʿōlām

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r6.claim: Syriac ʿâlam ʿâlmīn could nonetheless evoke the Greek liturgical formula eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn, meaning eternally.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r6.anchor: Doch figuriert syrisch ʿâlam ʿâlmīn im Sinne von griechisch eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn (»in alle Ewigkeit«) so prominent in der Liturgie

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r7.claim: Although ʿālamīn’s sound plural cannot mean worlds morphologically, it can designate a collective of people.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r7.anchor: wenn auch die »gesunde Pluralform« die einzig haltbare Deutung im Sinne von einem Personenkollektiv andeutet

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r8.claim: The form may be a cross-language wordplay presenting the emerging community as citizens of both worlds, through a nisba formation from ʿālam and rabbinic Hebrew ʿōlām.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r8.anchor: Es dürfte hier aber ein sprachenübergreifendes Wortspiel vorliegen, das die Menschen in der Phase der Herausbildung des neuen Gottesvolkes

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r9.claim: This theological lexicon recasts the negatively charged early Meccan human as homo eschatologicus, belonging to both worlds under God’s rule.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r9.anchor: Der in Frühmekka durchweg negativ konnotierte Mensch (al-insān, siehe etwa Q 103) wird mit der Einführung des Kollektivs al-ʿālamīn

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r10.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r10.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r10.claim: To preserve the eschatological dimension, translate rabb al-ʿālamīn as Lord of the worlds, with people implied; translate it simply as people where that reference is explicit.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:2:kommentar/r10.anchor: Will man bei rabb al-ʿālamīn die über eine bloße Autoritätsangabe hinausgehende eschatologische Dimension nicht unterschlagen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r1.claim: Praise can be given for beauty or good whether voluntary or not, whereas hamd is for good and beauty arising from will and choice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r1.anchor: hamd ancak irade ve istekle hâsıl olan iyilik ve güzellik karşısında yapılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r2.claim: Thanks is a verbal or practical response to intentional kindness and a moral duty toward benefactors, human or divine; hamd is spoken praise for all willful goodness, not only gifts.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r2.anchor: Şükür ve teşekkür “isteyerek yapılmış (ihtiyarî) bir iyilik ve ihsana karşı dille veya başka şekillerde uygun mukabelede bulunmak”tır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r3.claim: Hamd in its complete sense belongs only to God: human good is never fully independent of divine will, while unchosen gifts and qualities are directly the Creator’s work.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r3.anchor: bu mânada hamdin tamamı Allah’a mahsustur, O’na aittir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r4.claim: All created things in the material and spiritual, visible and unseen worlds, in this life and the hereafter, are included in the worlds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r4.anchor: Âlem maddî ve mânevî, görülen ve görülemeyen, dünyada ve âhirette Allah Teâlâ’nın yarattığı her şeydir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r5.claim: The visible domain is called the realm of dominion and witness, while immaterial existence is the unseen and angelic realm; God alone owns the latter, though worldly ownership can appear to belong to others.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r5.anchor: Görülen, hissedilen, insan bilgisinin ulaşabildiği maddî varlıklara “mülk ve şehâdet âlemi”, madde ötesi varlıklara da “gayb ve melekût âlemi” denilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r6.claim: Revelation compares the visible realm to a drop in the sea and a grain of sand beside the unseen; knowledge of cosmic scale points both to the limits of reason and the immensity of divine creation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r6.anchor: şehâdet ve mülk âlemi, gayb ve melekût âlemine nisbetle denizden bir damla, sahradan bir kum tanesi kadardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r7.claim: Contemplating the unseen’s immensity through faith leads from awe at God’s greatness to prostration and then to peace, security, love, nearness, and contentment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r7.anchor: bu azamet karşısında kul secdeye kapanınca onun hayret hali, “huzur, güven, sevgi, yakınlık ve tatmin”e dönüşmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r8.claim: Used alone, Rabb refers only to God and names His ownership and nurturing; in a construct such as master of a house, it can refer to others.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:2/r8.anchor: Rab kelimesi tek başına söylendiği zaman bundan yalnızca “Allah” kastedilir

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r1.claim: Most authorities say the Opening was revealed in Mecca and was among the Qur'an's earliest revelations.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r1.anchor: اختلفوا فيها فعند الأكثرين هي مكية من أوائل ما نزل من القرآن

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r2.speaker: أبو ميسرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r2.claim: Abu Maysara reports that before revelation the Prophet fled when a caller addressed him; Waraqa advised him to stay and listen, after which the call instructed him to attest to God's oneness and Muhammad's messengerhood and recite the Opening.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r2.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا برز سمع مناديا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r3.claim: Ali reports that the Opening descended in Mecca from a treasure beneath the Throne.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r3.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام قال: نزلت فاتحة الكتاب بمكة من كنز تحت العرش

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet recited the basmala and the Opening in Mecca, Quraysh responded with a curse or similar insult.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قام النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بمكة فقال: {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين}

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r5.claim: Mujahid alone says the Opening is Medinan; al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl calls this an isolated slip against the scholarly majority.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r5.anchor: وعند مجاهد أن الفاتحة مدنية. قال الحسين بن الفضل: لكل عالم هفوة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r6.speaker: الواحدي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi argues it must be Meccan because the Meccan Hijr 15:87 calls the seven oft-repeated a gift to the Prophet; it is unreasonable to say he prayed for over a decade without the Opening.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r6.anchor: ومما يقطع به على أنها مكية قوله تعالى: {ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني والقرآن العظيم} يعني: الفاتحة.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after Ubayy recited the Opening, the Prophet said no comparable surah was revealed in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an, calling it the seven oft-repeated and mighty Qur'an given to him.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وقرأ عليه أبي بن كعب أم القرآن، فقال:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r1.claim: The author opens the book with al-Fatiha for blessing.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r2.claim: Hamd is praise of beauty, whether a quality or gift, with love and reverence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r2.anchor: معنى {الحمد} : الثناءُ على الجميل من نعمةٍ أو غيرها مع المحبة والإجلال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r3.claim: Hamd covers praise of intrinsic qualities and beneficence, and is directed only to a living, rational being.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r4.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r4.claim: Madḥ is broader than hamd because one may praise beautiful pearls or jewels, but cannot give them hamd.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p11/r4.anchor: جاء في تفسير الرازي: "إن المدحَ قد يحصل للحي ولغير الحي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r1.claim: One distinction says hamd follows a real benefaction or praiseworthy quality, while madḥ may precede any good deed or be undeserved.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r1.anchor: إن المدحَ قد يكون قبل الإحسان، وقد يكون بعده، أما الحمد فإنه لا يكونُ إلا بعد الإحسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r2.speaker: النبي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r2.claim: The Prophet warns against excessive flatterers, supporting the distinction between deserved hamd and potentially misplaced madḥ.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r2.anchor: فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "احثُوا الترابَ في وجوه المَدَّاحين"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r3.speaker: النبي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r3.claim: The Prophet says that whoever does not praise people has not praised God, recognizing gratitude for people's real contributions.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r3.anchor: في حين قال: "مَنْ لم يَحمدِ الناسَ لم يحمدِ الله"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r4.claim: Al-hamd lillah implies that God is living, possesses perfect qualities, and does beautiful deeds and favors; madḥ lillah would not convey all this.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r4.anchor: علمنا من قوله: {الحمد للَّهِ} أنَّ الله حَيٌّ، له الصفات الحسنى والفعل الجميل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r5.claim: Hamd includes love, exaltation, and reverence beyond madḥ, making hamd the more fitting choice.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r5.anchor: في الحمد تعظيماً وإجلالاً ومحبة، ما ليس في المدح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r6.claim: Hamd applies whether a favor reaches the speaker or someone else, whereas shukr is limited to a favor received by the speaker.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p12/r6.anchor: إن الحمد يعمُّ ما إذا وصل ذلك الإنعامُ إليكَ أو إلى غيرك، وأما الشكر، فهو مختصٌّ بالإنعام الواصل إليك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r1.claim: One thanks a person only for a benefit received, but may praise that person's benefit to oneself or others.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r1.anchor: فأنتَ تشكر الشخص إذا أوصلَ إليك نعمةً، وأما الحمدُ فإنه لا يختص بذاك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r2.speaker: لسان العرب
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r2.claim: Hamd is more general than shukr: one praises intrinsic qualities and gifts, but does not thank someone for an intrinsic quality.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r2.anchor: جاء في (لسان العرب) : "والحمد والشكر متقاربان والحمدُ أعمّهما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r3.claim: Hamd is preferable to both madḥ and shukr because it covers God's qualities and favors to the speaker and all creation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r3.anchor: فكان اختيار (الحمد) أولى من المدح والشكر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r4.claim: The impersonal formula al-hamd lillah does not bind praise to a particular speaker, unlike I or we praise God, and presents God as universally praised.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p13/r4.anchor: في حين أن عبارة {الحمد للَّهِ} لا تختص بفاعل معين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r1.claim: Saying I praise God reports the speaker's act but does not establish that its object deserves praise; al-hamd lillah states God's entitlement without a specific speaker.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r1.anchor: إذا قلت: أحمد الله، أخبرتَ عن فعلك، ولا يعني ذلك أنَّ مَنْ تحمده يستحقُّ الحمد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r2.claim: The verb form is time-bound to the speaker's present or future, while al-hamd lillah leaves praise ongoing without a temporal limit.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r2.anchor: عبارة: {الحمد للَّهِ} مُطلقة غير مقيدة بزمن معين، ولا بفاعل معين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r3.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r3.claim: The formula means God was praised before any praiser or thanker and remains praised from eternity to eternity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p14/r3.anchor: جاء في (تفسير الرازي) : "إنه لو قال: (أحمدُ الله) ، أفاد ذلك كون ذلك القائل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r1.claim: A nominal sentence conveys established, lasting praise more strongly than a verbal sentence that suggests occurrence and renewal.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r1.anchor: الجملة الاسمية دالة على الثبوت، كما هو معلوم، وهي أقوى وأدوم من الفعلية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r2.claim: Al-hamd lillah declares praise to be God's due by His very essence and abundant favors, unlike a report that one person praises Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r2.anchor: ومنها: "أن قولنا: {الحمد للَّهِ} معناه: أن الحمد والثناء حقٌّ لله وملكه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r3.claim: Hamd is an inward recognition of a benefactor's favor and right to reverence; claiming I praise God can be false if the heart lacks that recognition, while the formula states a fact.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p15/r3.anchor: الحمدَ عبارة عن صفة القلب، وهي اعتقاد كون ذلك المحمود مُتفضِّلاً منعماً مستحقاً للتعظيم والإجلال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r1.claim: The contrast resembles the claim of testimony: one may lie about witnessing, as the hypocrites do, but the proposition that God alone is God remains true.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r1.anchor: ولهذا قال تعالى في تكذيب المنافقين: {والله يَشْهَدُ إِنَّ المنافقين لَكَاذِبُونَ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r2.claim: The nominative reading al-hamdu makes a nominal sentence and is stronger and more enduring than the accusative, which requires an implied verb.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r2.anchor: قراءة الرفع تدل على أن الجملة اسمية، في حين أن قراءة النصب، تدل على أن الجملة فعليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r3.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r3.claim: The nominative shift signals a settled meaning; the raised salam in Abraham's reply indicates a more enduring and complete greeting than theirs.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r3.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) : "والعدل بها عن النصب إلى الرفع على الابتداء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r4.speaker: البحر المحيط
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r4.claim: The seven readers agree on the nominative, which establishes praise; the accusative requires an implied agent and makes praise actor-specific and renewed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p16/r4.anchor: وجاء في (البحر المحيط) : "وقراءة الرفع أمكن في المعنى، ولهذا أجمع عليها السبعةُ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r1.speaker: البيضاوي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r1.claim: The nominative is chosen to convey praise's universality and permanence rather than a renewed event.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r1.anchor: وجاء في (تفسير البيضاوي) : "وإنما عدل عنه إلى الرفع، ليدلَّ على عموم الحمد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r2.claim: Even if the accusative is read as an imperative, commanding praise does not establish that the praised one deserves it; the nominative indicates deserved, established praise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r2.anchor: الأمر بالشيء، لا يعني أن المأمور به مستحق للفعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r3.claim: Al-hamdu lillah is a nominal and definite expression, unlike hamdan lillah; al can indicate known praise or all praise, while indefiniteness lacks this scope.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p17/r3.anchor: وإن (الحمد) مُعَرَّفةٌ بأل في حين أن (حمداً) نكرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r1.claim: Some take al as referring to the familiar praise among people, while others read it as encompassing every instance and kind of praise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r1.anchor: سبيل الاستغراق، فيدل على استغراق الأحمدة كلها. وَرجَّحَ بعضهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r2.claim: The author prefers both senses together: familiar praise belongs to God in a way that encompasses every kind and instance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r2.anchor: والراجحُ فيما يبدو لي، أن المعنيين مرادان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r3.claim: Most scholars treat al-hamd lillah as a report that praise is established for God; others call it performative praise, a transferred report, or a report that entails performance, and the author accepts both report and exaltation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p18/r3.anchor: وهذا هو الراجح في رأيي، فإنها تحتمل الخبر وإنشاء التعظيم، فتجمع المعنيين معاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p19/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p19/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p19/r1.claim: Al-hamd lillah is better than inna al-hamd lillah because believers do not doubt the claim, and the unmarked formula can report praise while enacting exaltation; inna makes it mere report.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p19/r1.anchor: إن عبارة: (الحمد لله) ، تحتمل الخبر وإنشاء التعظيم كما ذكرنا فتجمع المعنيين معاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p19/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p19/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p19/r2.claim: Al-hamd lillah is better than lillah al-hamd here: fronting lillah suggests exclusivity or rebuttal of doubt, neither of which fits this address to believers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p19/r2.anchor: إن المقامَ ليس مقام إزالة شك، ولا أنَّ هناك من ادّعى أن الحمد لغير الله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r1.claim: People may rightly praise others for favors; the hadith recognizes others' merit, while 3:188 condemns seeking praise for deeds not done.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r1.anchor: فإن حُمِدُوا بما فَعلوا، فلا بأس في ذلك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r2.claim: Al-hamd may appear to apply to God or another, so naming God clarifies it; worship can only be for God, so fronting You in 1:5 prevents an implication of worshipping another.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r2.anchor: جاء في تفسير الرازي ذِكْرُ الفرقِ بين قوله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r3.claim: Word order varies with context: al-Jathiya foregrounds God as deserving praise because it confronts disbelievers' false beliefs and denials of His lordship.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p20/r3.anchor: وإنما يكون ذلك بحسب المقام، فإذا اقتضى المقامُ التقديمَ، قُدِّمَ وإلا فلا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p21/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p21/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p21/r1.claim: Al-Jathiya answers denials of God's creative and beneficent lordship by showing Him as sole creator and provider, so He alone deserves praise; al-Fatiha addresses believers who seek steadfast guidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p21/r1.anchor: فهو وحده المتفضل على وجه الحقيقة، وهو المستحق الحمد على جهة الحصر والقصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p21/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p21/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p21/r2.claim: Al-Jathiya repeatedly uses restrictive constructions, matching its context of disbelievers who reject God and setting up its exclusive praise formula.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p21/r2.anchor: هذا من ناحية، ومن ناحية أخرى، إنَّ جُلَّ التعبيرات في سورة الجاثية، جرت على طريقة الحصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p22/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p22/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p22/r1.claim: The many restrictive statements throughout al-Jathiya culminate in exclusive praise and sovereignty for God, so its context calls for fronting Him as the one deserving praise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p22/r1.anchor: فاقتضى المقام تقديم الذات، المستحقة للحمد من كل ناحية في سورة الجاثية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r1.claim: Using God's proper name rather than an attribute avoids implying that He deserves praise only for one quality; the name points to His essence and entitlement across all attributes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r1.anchor: فجاء بالذات ليدل على أن الحمد إنما استحقه لذاته هو، لا بوصفٍ دون وصف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r2.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r2.claim: The proper name makes God's essence, rather than one particular quality, the ground of His right to praise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r2.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) : "أتى باسم الذات في الحمدلةِ لئلا يتوهم لو اقتصر على الصفة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r3.claim: Allah suits the following worship verse: on the prevalent etymology it derives from ilah, the worshipped, and the Qur'an often pairs this name with worship.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p23/r3.anchor: لأن هذا اللفظ على أشهر الأقوال مأخوذ من لفظ (الإله)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r1.claim: Even attributes such as Living or Knowing can describe others, and even unique descriptions may not explicitly identify God, so Allah is the clearest name.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r1.anchor: لم يفهم أن المقصود به الله صراحة، فكان ذكر (الله) أولى من ذكر أي اسم آخر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r2.claim: The verse's wording is preferable to the alternatives madḥ, shukr, I/we praise, an imperative, accusative praise, an indefinite praise, inna, fronted lillah, or a divine attribute.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r2.anchor: فتبين من هذا أن: {الحمد للَّهِ} أَوْلى من

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r3.claim: Rabb can mean owner, master, educator, guardian, and benefactor; the Lord of the worlds embodies these roles.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r3.anchor: الربُّ: المالك، والسيد، والمربّي والقيّم، والمنعم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r4.claim: An owner, master, and beneficent educator has a stronger claim to praise, and the Lord can direct His subjects as He wills.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p24/r4.anchor: وبُدئ بالرب، لأنه له التصرف في المَسُود والمملوك والعابد بما أراد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r1.claim: Rabb al-alamin subsumes many divine qualities, since each name or attribute governs what it describes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r1.anchor: ودخل تحت قوله: {رَبِّ العالمين} كثيرٌ من صفات الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r2.claim: Some limit al-alamin to knowledgeable or morally responsible creatures, citing its use for those who receive warning and recognize signs.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r2.anchor: فرجَّح بعضهم أنها تفيد ذوي العلم خاصة، أو المُكَلَّفين من الخَلْقِ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r3.claim: Some say al-alamin means humans, supported by Qur'anic references to men among the worlds and Israel receiving a distinction over them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إن العالمين هم الإنس بدليل قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r4.claim: One view takes the plural to include every kind, since humans, animals, insects, and each species may each be called a world.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r4.anchor: وقيل: جمع العالم ليشمل كل جنس مما سُمِّيَ به

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r5.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r5.claim: Another view says each generation or age is a world, so the plural encompasses all peoples and eras.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r5.anchor: وقيل: كل قرن وكل جيل يسمى عالَماً أيضاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r6.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r6.claim: Another explanation says the plural prevents al-alam from being understood only as the perceptible physical world, a common usage.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p25/r6.anchor: وقيل: جمعه لاحتمال أن ينصرف الذهن بلفظ (العالَم) إلى هذا العالم المحسوس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r1.claim: Since usage commonly narrows al-alam to the perceptible world, its plural can ensure comprehensive scope.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r1.anchor: لإلْفِ النفس بالمحسوسات فجمع ليفيد الشمول قطعاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r2.claim: Qur'anic uses show al-alamin can mean a generation or people of a particular time, including Israel, Mary, and the men addressed by Lot.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r2.anchor: والظاهر أنه يَصحُّ إطلاقُ لفظ (العالمين) على الجيل الواحد، أو الأجيال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r3.claim: Although some restrict worlds to accountable beings, Pharaoh's question is answered by describing the Lord of the worlds, not by defining the word worlds.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p26/r3.anchor: وقد خَصَّ هذه اللفظةَ بعضُ أهل العلم بالمكلفين خاصة، ورُدّ بقوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r1.claim: Moses' reply lists qualities of the Lord rather than defining al-alamin, just as calling a house's lord a merchant does not define the house.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r1.anchor: فليست كلمة (تاجر) أو (فقيه) أو (موظف) تفسيراً لـ (هذه الدار)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r2.claim: Al-awalim can include all beings, but al-alamin applies to rational beings or groups where rational creatures predominate, not to nonrational creatures alone.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r2.anchor: وإن (العالمين) لا تطلق إلا على ذوي العلم خاصة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r3.claim: This plural suits al-Fatiha because its worship, aid, guidance, and moral categories address accountable creatures; Rabb al-alamin may mean their Lord or all creation with rational beings predominant.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p27/r3.anchor: فكان هذا الاختيار أنسب شيء، ولو قال: رب العالم أو رب العوالم، لم يحسن هذا الحُسْنَ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r1.claim: Rabb al-alamin also answers Jews who claim God is Lord only of Israel: He is Lord of all humanity and accountable creatures.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r1.anchor: فيه رداً على المغضوب عليهم، ومنهم اليهود الذين يدّعون أن الله ربُّ بني إسرائيل خاصة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r2.claim: Al-Fatiha's concise Rabb al-alamin fits its focus on accountable creatures, whereas al-Jathiya explicitly names heaven and earth after repeatedly detailing their signs and God's rule over them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r2.anchor: كل مقام اقتضى التعبير الوارد فيه، فقد تردَّدَ ذِكْرُ السماوات والأرض، وما فيهن أكثر من مرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r3.claim: Al-Jathiya details God's lordship over humans and other living beings through creation, subjection, sustenance, and resurrection.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p28/r3.anchor: فقد سَخَّرَ اللهُ البحرَ وما في السماوات والأرض للإنسان، وهذا من مظاهر الربوبية له

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r1.claim: God's mercy toward believers and the laws sent to humanity also display His lordship; al-Fatiha names moral classes while al-Jathiya details the wider cosmos.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r1.anchor: وذكر الشرائع التي أنزلها الله على البشر، وهذا كله من مظاهر الربوبية للعالمين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r2.claim: The differing formulations of Rabb al-alamin and Lord of heaven, earth, and worlds each fit the focus of their surah.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r3.claim: Al-Jathiya mentions God's true sovereignty because it condemns arrogant mockers, while al-Fatiha has no such context and mentions only praise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p29/r3.anchor: فناسب ذلك أن يذكر أن له الكبرياء في السماوات والأرض

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p30/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p30/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p30/r1.claim: Other opening praises name God as creator, originator, owner of all things, or sender of scripture; each fits its surah and the openings complement one another.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p30/r1.anchor: غير أن الملاحظ أن هذه الافتتاحات متكاملة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p30/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p30/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p30/r2.claim: God originates heaven and earth from nothing, creates by measuring and shaping, owns them and their contents, sustains and repairs them, and sends scripture to guide creation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p30/r2.anchor: فبعد أن ذكر أنه فطر السماوات والأرض وخلقها، ذكرَ أن له ما فيها أيضاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r1.claim: These openings jointly describe God as originator, shaper, owner, sustainer, and guide through revealed books; Rabb al-alamin encompasses all these qualities and worlds.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r2.claim: Rabb highlights that creation depends on God not only when it begins but also while it continues, a dependence disputed for things in their state of persistence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r2.anchor: جاء في (تفسير الرازي) : "أنه تعالى لم يقل: الحمد لله خالق العالمين، بل {الحمد للَّهِ رَبِّ العالمين}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r3.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r3.claim: The next four opening praise formulas describe particular aspects contained in al-Fatiha's general Rabb al-alamin.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p31/r3.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى افتتح سوراً أربعة بعد هذه السورة بقوله: {الحمد للَّهِ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r1.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r1.claim: Al-Anam's creation of heaven and earth, darkness, and light is one part of the wider lordship over all worlds in al-Fatiha.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r1.anchor: فالمذكور في أول سورة الأنعام كأنه قسم من أقسام ما هو مذكور في أول سورة الفاتحة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r2.claim: Al-Kahf's revelation nurtures souls with knowledge, a particular form of the general nurture expressed by Rabb al-alamin.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r3.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r3.claim: Saba's statement that all in heaven and earth belongs to God is one aspect of al-Fatiha's general praise of the Lord of the worlds.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r3.anchor: وبَيَّنَ في أول سورة سبأ أن الأشياء الحاصلة في السماوات والأرض له

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r4.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r4.claim: Fatir's origination differs from Anam's creation by measure, yet both are aspects of Rabb al-alamin; Anam then mentions darkness and light, while Fatir mentions angels as messengers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p32/r4.anchor: والمذكور في هذه السورة كونه فاطراً لها ومحدثاً لذواتها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r1.claim: The pair of openings complement each other: Anam follows creation with light and darkness, while Fatir follows origination with the creation of spiritual messengers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r1.anchor: ذكر بعد خَلْق السماوات والأرض، جَعْلَ الأنوار والظلمات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r2.claim: Rabb al-alamin suits the request for guidance to the straight path because a nurturer's primary task is guidance, a frequent Qur'anic association.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r2.anchor: أن قوله: {رَبِّ العالمين} مناسب لقوله فيما بعد: {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p40/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p40/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p40/r1.claim: God is praiseworthy in His essence, lordship, rightly placed mercy, and ownership of Judgment Day; the sequence spans all times from eternity through the endless afterlife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p40/r1.anchor: وقد استغرق هذا الحمد الأزمنة كلها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r1.claim: The praise covers time from eternity to eternity, echoed by praise in the first and last life and at the end of judgment; this fullness makes al-Fatiha worthy to be the Mother of the Book.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r1.anchor: فاستغرق الحمد الزمان كلَّه من الأزل إلى الأبد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r2.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r2.claim: The names following praise show God is praiseworthy in divinity, lordship, mercy, and kingship.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r2.anchor: جاء في (التفسير القيم) : "في ذِكْرِ هذه الأسماء بعد الحمد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.claim: Invoking the congregation’s mercy, the worshipper praises, worships, seeks help, asks guidance, follows the righteous, and flees the rejected as a group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.anchor: سمعت رسولك يقول: (الجماعة رحمة والفرقة عذاب) فلما أردت تحميدك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r4.claim: Unrestricted praise and the enduring nominal descriptions of the angry and astray all suggest timeless, lasting states.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r4.anchor: أن الحمد مطلق غير مقيد بزمن ولا بفاعل معين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.claim: The surah gathers the foundations of Islamic belief: God and His perfect attributes, monotheism, the Last Day, divine power, and the messengers and revelation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.anchor: إن هذه السورة جمعت أصول العقيدة الإسلامية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r4.claim: God’s lordship over all entails that He alone is Lord, while exclusive worship and reliance affirm that there is no deity but Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r4.anchor: فإن كونه رباً للعالمين جميعاً، يعني: أنه لا رَبَّ سواه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r2.claim: Praise of God implies that a Creator exists, knows, has power, and deserves praise and glorification.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r2.anchor: فقوله {الحمد للَّهِ} يدل على وجود الصانع، وعلى علمه وقدرته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r3.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r3.claim: Lord of all worlds establishes God’s oneness and ownership of all creation, with no other lord or deity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r3.anchor: وأما قوله: {رَبِّ العالمين} فهو يدل على أن ذلك الإله واحد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r6.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r6.claim: Al-Razi summarizes praise as God’s existence and choice, lordship as unity, mercy as compassion in both worlds, and Judgment Day as wisdom and mercy.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r6.anchor: وقوله: {الرحمان الرحيم} يدل على رحمته في الدنيا والآخرة.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r8.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r8.claim: The surah is truly the Mother of the Book because it contains both doctrinal foundations and the two pillars of action.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r8.anchor: فهذه السورة هي أم الكتاب حقاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r1.claim: Hamd is heartfelt praise of a living, rational being's beautiful qualities or benefactions, with love and reverence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r1.anchor: الثناء على الجميل من النعمة أو غيرها مع المحبة والإجلال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r2.claim: Praise is broader than hamd: it may precede a good deed and may describe an inanimate object, while hamd requires actual merit and follows benefaction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r2.anchor: قد ثبت أن المدح أعم من الحمد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r3.claim: The Prophet warns against excessive flatterers, supporting the distinction between unearned praise and merited hamd.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r3.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:"احثوا التراب في وجه المداحين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r4.claim: The Prophet says that whoever fails to thank people has not thanked God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r4.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:"من لم يحمد الناس لم يحمد الله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r5.claim: Hamd is preferable to madḥ and shukr because it covers both God's intrinsic qualities and His benefactions, whereas shukr applies only to favors and madḥ need not reflect real merit.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r5.anchor: الحمد أعمهما لأنك تحمد الإنسان على صفاته الذاتية وعلى عطائه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r6.claim: The wording الحمد لله states that God merits praise for His qualities and deeds, whereas أحمد الله reports only the speaker's own act of praising.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p8/r6.anchor: في حين أن عبارة "الحمد لله" لا تختص بفاعل معين فهو المحمود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r1.claim: Unlike a first-person verb, الحمد لله is not limited to a speaker or to the finite time in which that person can praise; its praise is unceasing.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r2.claim: Al-Razi says أحمد الله declares the speaker able to praise, while الحمد لله says God was praised before any created praiser and remains praised eternally.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r2.anchor: جاء في تفسير الرازي أنه لو قال " احمد الله " أفاد ذلك كون القائل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r3.claim: The nominal الحمد لله conveys stable, lasting praise, unlike the verbal sentence أحمد الله, which suggests occurrence and renewal.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r3.anchor: الجملة الاسمية دالة على الثبوت وهي أقوى وأدوم من الجملة الفعلية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r4.claim: الحمد لله also declares praise to be God's rightful property because of His abundant favors; a personal act of praising does not assert this entitlement.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p9/r4.anchor: الحمد والثناء حق لله وملكه فانه تعالى هو المستحق للحمد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r1.claim: Because hamd is a state of the heart, someone saying أحمد الله without reverence may lie, whereas الحمد لله remains true whether or not the speaker is attentive.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r1.anchor: والحمد: عبارة عن صفة القلب وهي اعتقاد كون ذلك المحمود متفضلا منعما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r2.claim: The author compares this to لا إله إلا الله, which does not claim a personal act of witnessing; a hypocrite can lie by saying أشهد, as 63:1 states.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r3.claim: The nominative reading الحمدُ لله makes a stable nominal sentence; the accusative requires an implied verb and yields a verbal sentence or command, so the nominative is stronger.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r3.anchor: قراءة الرفع تدل على أن الجملة اسمية في حين أن قراءة النصب تدل على أن الجملة فعلية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r4.claim: Even if the accusative is construed as a command to praise, a command does not establish that its object deserves praise; the declarative nominative is preferable.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p10/r4.anchor: الأمر بالشيء لا يعني أن المأمور به مستحق للفعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r1.claim: Some take the definite article in الحمد as referring to the known praise among its hearers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r1.anchor: قد تكون لتعريف العهد فيكون المعنى: أن الحمد المعروف بينكم هو لله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r2.claim: Others take the article as generic and exhaustive, covering every kind and instance of praise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r2.anchor: وقد يكون لتعريف الجنس على سبيل الاستغراق فيدل على استغراق الأحمدة كلها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r3.claim: The author favors the exhaustive sense, supported by the Prophetic prayer اللهم لك الحمد كله: all known praise belongs to God without exception.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r3.anchor: "اللهم لك الحمد كله" فدل على استغراق الحمد كله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r4.speaker: أكثر النحاة والمفسرين
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r4.claim: Most grammarians and exegetes treat الحمد لله as a report that praise belongs to God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r4.anchor: قال أكثر النحاة والمفسرين: أن الحمد لله إخبار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r5.speaker: قسم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r5.claim: Another group treats the expression as performative because it embodies love.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r5.anchor: وقسم قال: أنها إنشاء لأن فيها استشعار المحبة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r6.speaker: قسم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r6.claim: A further view classifies it as a report that also contains a performative act.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r6.anchor: وقسم قال: أنها خبر يتضمن إنشاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r7.claim: The phrase can function as either report or invocation depending on context, letting the speaker affirm God's praise while expressing appreciation and reverence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r7.anchor: الحمد لله هي من العبارات التي يمكن أن تستعمل خبرا وإنشاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r8.claim: الحمد لله can carry both report and invocation, but إن الحمد لله forces a performative reading and loses that breadth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p11/r8.anchor: عندما تدخل عليه " إن " لا يمكن إلا أن يكون إنشاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r1.claim: Arabic particles can shift a phrase between invocation and report, as رحمه الله and رزقك الله differ from their versions introduced by قد.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r1.anchor: من المعلوم انه في اللغة قد تدخل بعض الأدوات على عبارات فتغير معناها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r2.claim: Fronting لله in لله الحمد normally marks restriction, but al-Fatiha's context is not one of exclusive praise: worldly praise can also be directed to people, unlike exclusive worship.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r2.anchor: الحمد في الدنيا قد تقال لأستاذ أو سلطان عادل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r3.claim: The context contrast explains the order: al-Fatiha has believers confessing worship and asking for help, while al-Jathiya answers unbelievers' claims about life and death by foregrounding God's praise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p12/r3.anchor: أما في سورة الجاثية فالمقام في الكافرين وعقائدهم وقد نسبوا الحياة والموت لغير الله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r1.claim: Al-Jathiya repeatedly discusses God's lordship over the heavens, earth, creation, and worlds; its closing praise gathers these themes, unlike al-Fatiha's focus on the worlds and their accountable groups.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r1.anchor: جمع الربوبية في السموات والأرض والعالمين في آية واحدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r2.claim: Al-Jathiya's mention of divine majesty in heaven and earth answers the arrogant rejecters described in 45:7–9; al-Fatiha has no corresponding context of arrogance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r2.anchor: دل على مظهر من مظاهر الاستكبار لذا ناسب أن يرد ذكر الكبرياء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r3.claim: Using God's proper name means He deserves praise for His essence, not merely for one attribute such as power or creation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p13/r3.anchor: عند ذكر الذات (الله) فإنها تعني انه سبحانه يستحق الحمد لذاته لا لوصفه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r1.claim: The name Allah suits the move to worship because it denotes the deity to be worshipped, and the author says it is paired with worship more than fifty times in the Quran.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r1.anchor: لفظ الجلالة (الله) يعنى الإله المعبود مأخوذة من أله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r2.claim: Rabb al-alamin is the apt continuation after praise: Rabb means owner, master, educator, benefactor, and caretaker, and encompasses God's attributes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r2.anchor: الرب هو المالك والسيد والمربي والمنعم والقيِّم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r3.claim: The author says al-alamin is suited to accountable and rational beings, unlike awalim, which can name classes of animals, insects, or inanimate things.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p14/r3.anchor: اختيار العالمين على العوالم أمر بلاغي يعني ذلك أن العالمين خاص للمكلفين وأولي العقل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r1.claim: Al-alamin may refer to all accountable generations or a subset, as in Lot's people; it fits al-Fatiha's concern with guidance and human moral groups and answers Jews who claimed God only as their Lord.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r1.anchor: جاءت رب العالمين لتشمل كل العالمين لا بعضهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r2.claim: Rabb also fits the request for guidance because education is a core sense of lordship and guidance frequently follows the name Rabb in scripture.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r2.anchor: من معاني الرب المربي وهي أشهر معانيه وأولى مهام الرب الهداية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p18/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p18/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p18/r4.claim: The sequence praises God for His essence, lordship, properly placed mercy, and ownership and kingship on the day of recompense.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p18/r4.anchor: محمود في رحمته يضعها حيث يجب أن توضع وهو محمود يوم الدين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r1.claim: The opening attributes span all time: praise before creation, at creation, through continuing mercy, and through the unending recompense of the afterlife, as 28:70 says.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r1.anchor: استغرق الحمد كل الأزمنة من الأزل إلى الأبد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.claim: The guidance request ties the chapter together: Rabb guides, Rahman and Rahim show mercy, worship and reliance require the path, and the favored oppose the astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.anchor: هذا الدعاء ارتبط بأول السورة وبوسطها وآخرها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.claim: Al-Fatiha contains faith and good works, affirming God, the Last Day, angels, messengers, and scriptures, and joins lordship's unity to the unity of worship; it is therefore the Mother of the Book.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه السورة توحيد الربوبية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r1.claim: Ḥamd is verbal praise for beauty, whether based on a blessing or not, spoken with the tongue; it is the opposite of blame.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r1.anchor: الحمد الثناء على الجميل من نعمة أو غيرها باللسان وحده، ونقيضه الذم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says ḥamd is a metathesized form of madḥ; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this despite their parallel inflection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r2.anchor: وليس مقلوب مدح، خلافا لابن الأنباري، إذ هما في التصريفات متساويان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r3.claim: Three positions equate praise and thanks, make ḥamd broader, or distinguish thanks for deeds from praise for attributes; Abū Ḥayyān prefers ḥamd as broader.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r3.anchor: والحمد والشكر بمعنى واحد، أو الحمد أعم، والشكر ثناء على الله تعالى بأفعاله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r4.claim: The lām in lillāh has numerous possible relations, including ownership, entitlement, relation, cause, communication, specification, outcome, time, endpoint, and elevation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r4.anchor: لله اللام: للملك وشبهه، وللتمليك وشبهه، وللاستحقاق، وللنسب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r5.claim: Rabb may mean master, owner, abiding one, worshipped one, or reformer; some also understand companion or creator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r5.anchor: الرب: السيد، والمالك، والثابت، والمعبود، والمصلح، وزاد بعضهم بمعنى الصاحب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for two scopes of al-ʿālamīn: every living being, or humans, jinn, and angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r6.anchor: ومدلوله كل ذي روح، قاله ابن عباس، أو الناس، قاله البجلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r7.speaker: البجلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r7.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، أو الناس، قاله البجلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya restricts al-ʿālamīn to the two responsible kinds, humans and jinn.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة والفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r9.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Farrāʾ include humans, jinn, angels, and devils in al-ʿālamīn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r9.anchor: أو الإنس والجن والملائكة والشياطين، قاله أبو عبيدة والفراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r10.claim: Other reported scopes include Adam's children, the people of Paradise and Hell, all recipients of provision, every made thing, and spiritual beings; Abū Ḥayyān leaves the correct count to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r10.anchor: أو بنو آدم، قاله أبو معاذ، أو أهل الجنة والنار، قاله الصادق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r11.claim: The majority pronounce the dāl of al-ḥamdu with ḍamma.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r12.speaker: إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r12.claim: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla harmonizes the mīm's vowel with the following lām's ḍamma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r12.anchor: وأتبع إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة ميمه لام الجر لضمة الدال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r13.speaker: الحسن وزيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Zayd ibn ʿAlī harmonize the dāl's kasra with the lām's kasra, a stranger kind of agreement between inflectional and non-inflectional vowels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p32/r13.anchor: كما أتبع الحسن وزيد بن علي كسرة الدال لكسرة اللام، وهي أغرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r1.speaker: هارون العتكي، ورؤبة، وسفيان بن عيينة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r1.claim: Hārūn al-ʿAtakī, Ruʾba, and Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna read al-ḥamda in the accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r1.anchor: وقرأ هارون العتكي، ورؤبة، وسفيان بن عيينة الحمد بالنصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r2.claim: The definite article on ḥamd may indicate a known instance, the abstract quality, or the entire genus of praise; the last implies exhaustive praise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r2.anchor: إما للعهد، أي الحمد المعروف بينكم لله، أو لتعريف الماهية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r3.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r3.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī records the plural aḥmad for ḥamd, as if accounting for its varied kinds, and Abū Ḥayyān quotes a poetic example.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r3.anchor: وحكى ابن الأعرابي: جمعه على أحمد كأنه راعى فيه جامعه اختلاف الأنواع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r4.claim: The nominative reading is semantically stronger and unanimously adopted by the Seven because it states that praise is established for God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r4.anchor: وقراءة الرفع أمكن في المعنى، ولهذا أجمع عليها السبعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r5.claim: The accusative reading needs an implied governor such as I praise God or I praised God; it presents praise as newly occurring and names its agent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r5.anchor: ومن نصب، فلا بد من عامل تقديره أحمد الله أو حمدت الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r6.claim: Among proposed governors for the accusative, Abū Ḥayyān prefers the explicit-sense verb ahmadu over a command or other unexpressed verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r6.anchor: وقدّر بعضهم العامل للنصب فعلا غير مشتق من الحمد، أي أقول الحمد لله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r7.claim: With the accusative, lillāh is an explanatory lām; it cannot be governed by the verbal noun, as the Arabic construction saqyan li-Zayd shows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r7.anchor: وفي قراءة النصب، اللام للتبيين، كما قال أعني لله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي وطائفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r8.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī and a group read rabb al-ʿālamīn in the accusative as praise, though lowering the following epithets weakens the construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r8.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وطائفة رب العالمين بالنصب على المدح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r9.speaker: الأهوازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r9.claim: Al-Ahwāzī records Zayd ibn ʿAlī reading rabb, raḥmān, and raḥīm all in the accusative, which removes the syntactic weakness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r9.anchor: على أن الأهوازي حكى في قراءة زيد بن علي أنه قرأ رب العالمين، الرحمن الرحيم بنصب الثلاثة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects deriving the accusative rabb from a prior implied verb such as We praise God, since this analogy to ellipsis in coordination is not productive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p34/r10.anchor: وقول من زعم أنه نصب رب بفعل دل عليه الكلام قبله، كأنه قيل نحمد الله رب العالمين، ضعيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p35/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p35/r1.claim: Rabb is a verbal noun used adjectivally in one analysis, or an active participle with its alif omitted, like barr from bārr.
